business_quality_reasoning: Coverall is a very young company (incorporated July 2024) with only 7 Google reviews, so it is trading but unproven. The 4.9 rating and a London-wide cleaning offer show a real commercial intent, but the thin web presence suggests early-stage revenue.
price_point_reasoning: Window and domestic cleaning jobs in London typically run £30-£80 per visit; no prices are shown on the site so the category midpoint is used.
modernity_gap: The design language is recent (Webflow, 2024 copyright), but the page is essentially a single hero and contact button with no services, proof or content beneath it — it reads like an unfinished site rather than a dated one.
site_weaknesses: The entire homepage is a hero image, one paragraph and a Contact Us button — no services, prices, areas covered or process are explained
No reviews, testimonials, accreditations or team photos — nothing proves this is a real, trusted business
Only one CTA (Contact Us) with no phone number, quote form or booking option visible on the page
Below the hero the desktop capture is essentially empty dark imagery — sections either missing or failing to render
No content for Google to rank beyond a single sentence, so the site is invisible for local search terms
site_analysis: The site looks like a half-finished Webflow build: a moody hero with 'Cleaning Services Across London' and a contact button, then effectively nothing. There are no service descriptions, no pricing, no reviews and no proof the business exists — a visitor has no reason to trust it or any information to act on. For a company chasing London cleaning work, the site converts almost nobody because there is nothing to convert with.
review_summary: Your website looks smart at the top, but there is almost nothing behind it — no list of what you clean, no prices, no reviews and no photos of your work. A customer landing here has to take a leap of faith to contact you, and most will not. Adding your services, a few real reviews and a clear way to get a quote would turn this page into something that actually wins you jobs.
outreach_angle: Your homepage promises 'cleaning services across London' but never says what you actually clean — visitors have to guess before they can enquire.
